sentences.text: **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**
Context or background.
The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was enacted in 2005.
It aims to provide legal guarantee for at least 100 days of unskilled wage employment in a financial year to every rural household.
The scheme was introduced to enhance livelihood security in rural areas.
It seeks to create durable assets and improve the economic and social conditions of rural households.
MGNREGA is a demand-driven scheme that empowers rural citizens.
Objectives.
The primary objective of MGNREGA is to enhance livelihood security in rural areas.
It aims to provide at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year to every rural household.
The scheme also focuses on creating durable assets in rural areas.
It seeks to improve the economic and social conditions of rural households.
MGNREGA promotes the right to work and helps in reducing rural poverty.
Benefits and assistance.
Under MGNREGA, every rural household is entitled to 100 days of unskilled wage employment per financial year.
Wages are paid according to the minimum wage rate fixed by the state government.
The scheme provides a safety net for rural households during lean agricultural seasons.
It helps in the creation of community assets such as roads, ponds, and irrigation facilities.
MGNREGA also promotes social inclusion by providing employment to marginalized groups.
Eligibility.
All rural households are eligible to apply for employment under MGNREGA.
There is no restriction on the number of applications from a household.
The scheme is applicable to all states and union territories in India.
Households must register under the scheme to avail of the benefits.
Individuals must be willing to work for unskilled manual labor.
Application process.
To apply for MGNREGA, households must submit an application to the local Gram Panchayat.
The application must include details of the household members seeking employment.
Once registered, the household will receive a job card.
The job card serves as proof of registration and entitlement to work.
Households can request work by submitting a written application to the Gram Panchayat.
Timeline or frequency.
MGNREGA operates throughout the year.
Employment can be sought at any time during the financial year.
The scheme guarantees 100 days of wage employment per household in a financial year.
Wages are paid within 15 days of the completion of work.
The scheme is reviewed and updated annually.
Implementing authorities or agencies.
The Ministry of Rural Development is the nodal ministry for MGNREGA.
State governments are responsible for the implementation of the scheme.
Gram Panchayats play a crucial role in the execution of MGNREGA projects.
Local authorities are responsible for monitoring and evaluating the work done under the scheme.
The scheme is supported by various government departments at the state and central levels.
Other available details.
MGNREGA promotes transparency and accountability through social audits.
The scheme encourages participation of the local community in planning and implementation.
It also provides for the establishment of a grievance redressal mechanism.
MGNREGA has provisions for the inclusion of women and marginalized groups.
The scheme has been instrumental in reducing rural distress and migration.
**Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**
Context or background.
The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana was launched in 2015.
It aims to provide affordable housing to the urban poor.
The scheme is part of the government's initiative to ensure housing for all by 2022.
PMAY focuses on providing pucca houses with basic amenities.
Objectives.
The primary objective of PMAY is to provide affordable housing to the urban poor.
It aims to construct 20 million affordable houses by 2022.
The scheme seeks to promote sustainable and inclusive urban development.
PMAY also aims to enhance the quality of life for urban residents.
Benefits and assistance.
Under PMAY, beneficiaries receive financial assistance for the construction or purchase of a house.
The scheme provides interest subsidy on home loans for eligible beneficiaries.
The subsidy is applicable for loans up to ₹2.67 lakh.
Beneficiaries can avail of a credit-linked subsidy scheme.
The scheme also provides for the construction of houses with basic amenities.
Eligibility.
The scheme is targeted at Economically Weaker Sections and Low-Income Groups.
Beneficiaries must have an annual income of up to ₹3 lakh for EWS.
For LIG, the annual income limit is up to ₹6 lakh.
Applicants must not own a pucca house in their name or in the name of any family member.
Eligibility is determined based on the income and housing status of the applicant.
Application process.
To apply for PMAY, beneficiaries must visit the official PMAY website.
They can also apply through Common Service Centers or designated banks.
The application requires submission of income proof and identity documents.
Beneficiaries must provide details of the existing housing status.
Applications are processed based on eligibility criteria set by the government.
Timeline or frequency.
PMAY is an ongoing scheme with no specific end date.
Applications can be submitted at any time during the year.
The construction of houses is expected to be completed within a stipulated timeframe.
The scheme is reviewed periodically to assess progress and impact.
Beneficiaries are informed about the status of their application within a specified period.
Implementing authorities or agencies.
The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs is the nodal ministry for PMAY.
State governments are responsible for implementing the scheme at the state level.
Urban local bodies play a crucial role in the execution of PMAY projects.
The scheme is supported by various financial institutions and banks.
Monitoring and evaluation are conducted by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
Other available details.
PMAY promotes the use of eco-friendly and sustainable building materials.
The scheme encourages the participation of private developers in housing projects.
It also provides for the development of infrastructure and amenities in housing projects.
PMAY has provisions for the inclusion of women and marginalized groups.
The scheme aims to create a sustainable urban environment through affordable housing.
**National Food Security Act (NFSA)**
Context or background.
The National Food Security Act was enacted in 2013.
It aims to provide subsidized food grains to approximately two-thirds of India's population.
The Act seeks to ensure food and nutritional security for all citizens.
NFSA is a significant step towards achieving the right to food.
Objectives.
The primary objective of NFSA is to provide subsidized food grains to eligible households.
It aims to ensure access to adequate food at affordable prices.
The Act seeks to improve the nutritional status of vulnerable sections of society.
NFSA also aims to promote the availability of food grains in the country.
Benefits and assistance.
Under NFSA, eligible households receive food grains at subsidized rates.
The scheme provides 5 kg of food grains per person per month.
Households are categorized into priority and general categories.
Priority households receive food grains at a highly subsidized rate of ₹3 per kg for rice, ₹2 per kg for wheat, and ₹1 per kg for coarse cereals.
The Act also provides for the implementation of various nutritional programs.
Eligibility.
Eligibility for NFSA is determined based on the socio-economic status of households.
Priority households include those belonging to the below-poverty-line category.
The scheme also covers specific vulnerable groups such as pregnant women and lactating mothers.
State governments are responsible for identifying eligible households.
The criteria for eligibility may vary from state to state.
Application process.
To apply for NFSA, households must submit an application to the local authorities.
The application requires details of household members and income status.
Once verified, eligible households are issued a ration card.
The ration card serves as proof of entitlement to subsidized food grains.
Households can also check their eligibility status online.
Timeline or frequency.
NFSA is an ongoing scheme with no specific end date.
Food grains are distributed on a monthly basis to eligible households.
The scheme is reviewed periodically to assess its impact and effectiveness.
The distribution of food grains is conducted through the Public Distribution System.
Households can avail of benefits throughout the year.
Implementing authorities or agencies.
The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution is the nodal ministry for NFSA.
State governments are responsible for implementing the Act at the state level.
The Food Corporation of India plays a crucial role in the procurement and distribution of food grains.
Local authorities are responsible for monitoring the distribution process.
The scheme is supported by various government departments and agencies.
Other available details.
NFSA promotes transparency and accountability through the use of technology.
The Act provides for the establishment of grievance redressal mechanisms.
It encourages the participation of civil society organizations in monitoring the implementation.
NFSA has provisions for the inclusion of women and marginalized groups.
The scheme aims to create a food-secure nation through comprehensive food policies.
